content.text: YouBuyy stores product master data in a MySQL DB. This data must be ingested into a Kafka Topic for other services to consume.

items: Kafka distributes partitions among consumers.

subsections.heading: 1. Differences Between Apache Kafka and Confluent Kafka

items: Apache Kafka is the open-source core project used for building real-time streaming pipelines.

Confluent Kafka is a commercial distribution by Confluent Inc. It builds on Apache Kafka and adds features like Confluent Control Center (UI), Schema Registry, kSQL (SQL for streaming), pre-built connectors, enterprise-grade security (RBAC, audit logging), and 24/7 support.
Use case: Apache Kafka is suitable for DIY setups, while Confluent is ideal for enterprise deployments needing monitoring, security, and scaling tools.

subsections.heading: 2. Compare Apache Kafka, Amazon Kinesis, Google Pub/Sub, ActiveMQ

items: Apache Kafka: Distributed, high-throughput pub-sub system. Ideal for real-time analytics and event streaming. Self-managed or cloud-hosted.
Amazon Kinesis: AWS-native stream processing service. Easy integration with AWS ecosystem, serverless scaling.
Google Pub/Sub: Global, scalable messaging middleware. Push/pull support, integrates with Google Cloud.
ActiveMQ: Traditional message broker using JMS. Best for message queuing, not optimized for big data streaming.

content.text: Example: Use Kafka or Kinesis for large-scale analytics, Pub/Sub for global event distribution, ActiveMQ for reliable message queuing in enterprise apps.
